title: sourcing-battlecard-sla-clause-library-for-dedicated-gpu
content:
Audience: procurement owners, platform architects, legal counsel, field sales.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Purpose: give sales, solutions, and procurement a compact battlecard + clause library to close dedicated capacity deals where customers require predictable throughput, tenant isolation, and contractual remedies.
- Outcome: standard phrasing for throughput floors, isolation guarantees, incident credits, warm-standby options, and an operational playbook that buyers can take to legal.
- Status: working draft for field review; contains sample redlines for negotiation.

Positioning statement (single line):
Redwood Dedicated — predictable inference economics with engineering-grade isolation and contractual remedies that let platform teams buy confidence, not just GPUs.

Why this matters to buyers (bullet points):
- Predictability: predictable per-second throughput and capacity planning reduces overprovisioning and cloud waste.
- Risk transfer: explicit isolation and failover commitments shift operational risk away from customers during peak events.
- Procurement friendliness: ready-to-use clause templates accelerate legal review cycles.

Key messaging pillars for field:
1) Measured throughput guarantees — not vague SLAs. We commit to throughput floors by SKU and offer baseline/peak bands with objective measurement methods.
2) Isolation that matters — tenant-level resource isolation + data plane separation and optional VPC/private control-plane.
3) Graceful degradation policies — model-variant fallbacks and routing policies that keep apps online with fidelity guarantees.
4) Operational contracts — runbooks, escalation targets, and financial credits tied to measurable SLOs.

Competitive differentiators to call out during procurement conversations:
- Multi-tier fallback model strategy: automatic downgrade to quantized/compatible variants with fidelity thresholds (vs. competitors that only throttle).
- Prefix/KV caching transparency: we expose cache hit metrics and offer caching SLAs for repeat prompt patterns.
- Private deployment parity: same API and rollout tooling across hosted, dedicated, and private (some rivals fragment behaviors by deployment mode).

Concise technical definitions buyers will ask for (use these exact lines):
- Throughput floor: minimum sustained tokens-per-second measured at the dedicated pool egress for a 1-hour rolling window.
- Tail latency SLO: 99.9th percentile end-to-end token latency measured at the API gateway.
- Isolation boundary: the set of controls and artifacts that prevent noisy neighbor interference (GPU tenancy, network ACLs, metadata separation, and per-tenant KV caches).
- Operational credit: financial remedy computed as (monthly committed fee) * (credit percentage), subject to measurement windows and caps.

Sample clause snippets (procurement-ready; copy/paste starting points):
1) Throughput commitment (baseline + burst):
"Provider shall maintain a baseline throughput of X tokens/sec for Customer's Dedicated Pool, measured as the average sustained throughput across any contiguous 60-minute window. Provider shall allow bursts up to Y tokens/sec for up to Z minutes per day. Failure to meet the baseline shall entitle Customer to operational credits as specified in the Credits Schedule."

2) Isolation guarantee: 
"Provider will maintain dedicated GPU tenancy and network segmentation for Customer's Dedicated Pool. Provider will not co-locate third-party tenant workloads on the same physical GPU hosts as Customer's Dedicated Pool unless explicitly agreed in writing. Provider will maintain separation of per-tenant KV caches and logging streams. Any breach of the Isolation Boundary clause entitles Customer to patch remediation and credits as defined in the Incident Credits section."

3) Fallback and fidelity: 
"Provider will implement automatic model-variant fallback to compatible quantized or lower-cost model variants during capacity constraints. Provider will maintain fidelity thresholds (e.g., BLEU/ROUGE/embedding cosine ranges or customer-provided samples) and will attempt fallbacks only if fidelity thresholds are met. If fallback results in fidelity outside agreed thresholds, the event is considered a Service Degradation."

4) Measurement and dispute:
"Throughput, latency, and cache metrics shall be published via Provider's Console and API. In case of disagreement, both parties will use mutually agreed metric definitions and a third-party measurement run (execution harness defined in Appendix A) to reconcile."

5) Credits and remedies: 
"Operational credits will be applied as a percentage of the monthly Dedicated Fee according to the following bands: Minor Degradation (credits 2.5%), Major Degradation (credits 10%), Outage (credits 25%). Credits are capped at 50% per billing period. Remedies exclude indirect damages and do not affect Customer's right to terminate for repeated failures as defined in the Termination for Cause clause."

Negotiation playbook for field reps (short steps):
- Stage 1 (Discovery): quantify 7- and 30-day peak patterns, percent of requests that must be within the Tail Latency SLO, and which workloads can tolerate fallback models.
- Stage 2 (Offer): propose baseline throughput + burst windows and a warm-standby option (see pricing appendix).
- Stage 3 (Legal): push operational credits instead of large termination penalties; credits buy time and leverage for engineering fixes.
- Stage 4 (Onboarding): final runbook workshop to map monitoring, alerts, and escalation contacts; store runbook in shared Confluence page.

Procurement checklist (hand this to buyers):
- Required: baseline throughput (tokens/sec), 99.9% tail latency target, isolation boundary description, measurement dashboard access, runbook and escalation contacts.
- Recommended: warm standbys, burst absorption minutes, fallback fidelity SLA, monthly run-rate credits, optional disaster-recovery region reservation.
- Nice-to-have: on-call rotation overlap during rollout, audit logs export cadence, KMS/HSM keywrap integration note.

Operational playbook excerpt (what SREs will do if SLOs breach):
1) Triage: validate metric via Console -> check pool utilization, KV cache hit rate, host-level telemetry.
2) Immediate mitigations: enable model-variant fallback, temporarily increase burst capacity (if available), route non-critical routes to cheaper pool.
3) Customer comms: notify customers within 15 minutes with incident severity, expected mitigation, and ETA.
4) Postmortem and credit calc: complete RCA within 7 business days, propose credits per agreed bands, publish runbook updates.

Simple competitive scoring (use in sales calls):
Criteria / Redwood / PublicCloudX / ModelAPI / InfraRun
Predictable throughput / High (measured floors + bursts) / Medium (best-effort) / Low (no guarantees) / Medium
Isolation / High (tenant GPU + network + cache) / Low (shared hosts) / Medium / Medium
Fallback fidelity / High (model variants + fidelity gating) / Low (throttle) / Medium / Low
Private deployment parity / Yes / Partial / No / Partial
Measurement transparency / Console + API / Limited / Console-only / Limited

Common buyer objections and scripts: 
- "Why not just provision more capacity?" => "Overprovisioning is expensive and brittle; dedicated contracts let you buy a predictable floor and use burst to handle spikes efficiently — we design commitment levels to reduce your unit costs while retaining headroom."
- "How do we trust the metrics?" => "We publish the same telemetry you’ll use in production; metrics are accessible via API and can be reconciled with an agreed harness (see linked artifacts)."
- "What if fallback reduces quality?" => "We only activate fallbacks when fidelity thresholds are met; fallback policies are configurable per-route and per-model."

Open questions for Legal & Product: (to resolve before finalizing template)
- Define exact measurement harness (appendix A) and agree on third-party runner for disputes.
- Decide on default credit bands and maximum cap by contract value.
- Warm-standby pricing and activation rules (automatic vs. customer-triggered).

Appendix (links + templates):
- SLA template (internal GH): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sla-templates/pull/22
- Measurement harness spec (Confluence-12345).
- Negotiation playbook card (internal Slack: #gtm-dedicated-ref).

Notes to field (short):
- Use this doc as a starting point — replace X/Y/Z with customer-specific numbers.
- For enterprise deals, push for runbook workshop before signature.
- If Legal asks to remove Isolation guarantee, escalate to Solutions Engineering for a technical compensating control proposal.
